newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER SHOWCASE-EKEREN CROWN SEASON OF UNDERDOGS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-EKEREN CROWN SEASON OF UNDERDOGS.

text.p: Ekeren's stunning 4-2 win over favourites Anderlecht in Sunday's Belgian cup final completed a coup by unfancied teams at the expense of the nation's traditional soccer powerhouses.
Ekeren lifted the first trophy in their history just a week after Lierse captured the league title, leaving Anderlecht and Club Brugge with UEFA Cup berths as consolation prize.
Standard Liege, the third of Belgium's top three sides, were left empty-handed.
Ekeren's win was a victory of grit and guile over money.
Dubbed by one newspaper as "the miracle of Belgian soccer", Ekeren have been ridiculed for their policy of signing veteran players in the twilight of their careers.

The small club from the suburbs of Antwerp, still buried in a regional division just 20 years ago, has however enjoyed its most successful season with an annual budget of only $2.0 million -- one-tenth of what Anderlecht has to spend.
Champions Lierse have a budget of $3.4 million.
"Admit it, we're not doing too badly with players from the rummage sale," Ekeren chairman Jos Verhaeghen said.
"The triumph of provincial clubs is remarkable because money is playing an ever-growing role in top soccer," daily Het Nieuwsblad newspaper said on Monday.
For the second time in a week, a club was hailed for its team and fighting spirit, compensating for a more modest measure of soccer technique.
"Ekeren like a diesel," Het Nieuwsblad said.
"Ekeren battles its way to cup," echoed Het Laatste Nieuws.
The plucky team, which arrived in Belgium's top flight only eight years ago, overcame a two-goal deficit to stun eight-times winners Anderlecht 4-2 after extra time on Sunday.
"Anderlecht were better but we continued to fight," Verhaeghen said.
"This is all down to our mentality," Ekeren defender Marc Schaessens added.

For Anderlecht, defeat capped a miserable season which had already been marred by match-fixing allegations and a ban on leading striker Gilles De Bilde who broke the nose and eye socket of an opponent by punching him during a match.
"This will always (be remembered) as a rotten season," Anderlecht chairman Roger Vanden Stock said.
Coach Johan Boskamp, due to join Ghent, added: "I can't tell you how disappointed I am...this is very bad, for myself but especially for the club."

Belgian media questioned whether Anderlecht were equipped to fight back next season. Four regulars, Bruno Versavel, Danny Boffin, Johan Walem and Nigerian international Celestine Babayaro, are leaving.

The success of Lierse and Ekeren was almost matched by the extraordinary rise of first division newcomers Mouscron, who led the league until February but faded after coach Georges Leekens was promoted to take charge of the national squad.
Mouscron finished third and will play in the UEFA Cup.
A fourth tiny club, Lommel, finished fifth and were denied a UEFA Cup berth only by Anderlecht's cup final defeat.
Ekeren coach Luc Verheyen said on Sunday his side were no longer "one of the little brothers" of Belgian soccer.
Many now wonder whether there are any big brothers left.
